Hence, distance between Stations Y and Z is **“60 km”**.

questions.question: A sum lent at simple interest amounts to Rs.6,240.80 in one year and to Rs.7,563.20 in 4 years. The sum (in Rs.) and the rate of interest per annum, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since Simple Interest is constant every year, SI for 3 years = Amount₄ − Amount₁

⇒ 3 years SI = 7563.20 − 6240.80 = ₹1322.40

⇒ 1 year SI = 1322.40 ÷ 3 = ₹440.80

⇒ Principal = 6240.80 − 440.80 = ₹5800

⇒ Rate = (440.80 ÷ 5800) × 100 = 7.6%

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5800, 7.6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 1 year (A₁) = ₹6240.80

Amount after 4 years (A₄) = ₹7563.20

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca7802c0f79cdccae092a74cb171e27c8b87cb65940ae2f9cfabbf71dfba811a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 3 years = A₄ − A₁

⇒ SI for 3 years = 7563.20 − 6240.80 = 1322.40

⇒ SI for 1 year = 1322.40 ÷ 3 = 440.80

⇒ Principal (P) = A₁ − SI for 1 year

⇒ P = 6240.80 − 440.80 = 5800

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ P

⇒ R = (440.80 × 100) ÷ 5800

⇒ R = 44080 ÷ 5800 = 7.6%

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5800, 7.6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant every year, meaning the interest generated is the same annually. In Compound Interest, the accumulated interest of past periods is added to the principal to form the base for the next period.

Principal from Amounts Rule

If a principal becomes A₁ in T₁ years and A₂ in T₂ years under Simple Interest, the principal can be directly calculated as P = A₁ − [ (A₂ − A₁) ÷ (T₂ − T₁) ] × T₁.

Constant SI Property

Since Simple Interest does not compound, the interest accrued over any N-year period is always directly proportional to N, making it uniformly additive.

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector-borne disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Malaria.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
 

 **Disease**
 **Details**
 
 

 Malaria
 
 
 
• It is a mosquito-borne infectious disease.
 
• It is caused by single-celled microorganisms of the plasmodium group.
 
• It is spread through the bites of infected **Anopheles** mosquitoes.
 
 
 
 

 Cholera
 
 
 
• It is an acute diarrheal illness.
 
• It is caused by the infection of the intestine with** Vibro Cholerae bacteria.**
 
 
 
 

 Pneumonia
 
 
 
• It is an infection in one or both lungs caused by **Bacteria, Viruses, Fungi.**
 
 
 
 

 Mumps
 
 
 
• It is caused by a family of viruses known as **paramyxoviruses**.
 
• The viral infection affects the salivary gland that is preventable by vaccine

questions.question: Which of the following soils is found in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Peaty soil.**__

__
 
• **Peaty soil is found in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 **Soil**
 **Details**
 
 

 Yellow soil
 
 
 
• It is formed under broad leaves in humid** subtropical regions.**
 
• Its yellow colour is due to ferric oxide
 
• It has an acid reaction and low humus content.
 
• Mainly found in Odisha and Chhattisgarh regions.
 
 
 
 

 Red soil 
 
 
 
• It develops in warm, temperate and humid climates.
 
• It contains thin organic mineral layers of highly leached soil resting on a red layer of alluvium
 
• Mainly found in Odisha and Chhattisgarh regions.
 
 
 
 

 Saline soil
 
 
 
• It contains a lower amount of Na adsorbed onto soil particles.
 
• They exist in arid and semi-arid regions in the regions of poor natural drainage
 
• It occurs in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Orissa, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat
 
 
 
 

 Peat soil
 
 
 
• It has a high water-holding capacity, high natural moisture content.
 
• It occurs in the northern part of Bihar, Southern part of Uttranchal, coastal areas of West Bengal, Orissa, Tamil Nadu
